strengths: The paper identifies two underexplored and reasonably well-motivated criteria for visual token pruning—intra-modal diversity and cross-modal task relevance—complementing the commonly used attention-based importance criterion. The motivating example (Figure 1) and empirical analysis (Figure 2, 'information migration') provide a clear rationale for the two-stage design.

The proposed method is training-free, architecture-agnostic, and simple to implement (greedy k-center selection + attention-ratio-based layer pruning), making it easy to adopt and compatible with efficient attention operators such as FlashAttention.

Extensive experiments across 12 benchmarks (8 image, 4 video) and two model scales (7B/13B) consistently show ToDRE outperforming several strong recent baselines (FastV, SparseVLM, FasterVLM, GlobalCom2) at multiple compression ratios, including under extreme 90% pruning.

Thorough ablations are provided, including the individual contribution of each stage, threshold sensitivity for layer selection, and choice of candidate layers, which support the design decisions and improve reproducibility.

Efficiency metrics (FLOPs, memory, throughput) are reported alongside accuracy, giving a fairly complete picture of the speed-performance trade-off, and qualitative case studies (Figures 6-7) help illustrate the intuitive benefit of diversity-driven retention over attention-driven pruning.
weaknesses: The theoretical justification in Appendix B for 'orthogonality' of intra- and cross-modal redundancy relies on a strong and largely unverified assumption (W_V^T W_T = 0) that visual and textual embeddings occupy strictly orthogonal subspaces within a shared LLM embedding space; this assumption is not empirically validated and is unlikely to hold exactly in real trained models, so the theoretical result provides limited practical insight beyond restating the intuition already given in Section 3.2.

The core techniques (greedy k-center diversity sampling, cross-modal attention ratio thresholding) are conceptually simple extensions/combinations of existing ideas (k-center clustering, VTW's information migration observation, [CLS]-attention pivot selection from FasterVLM); the novelty is more in careful engineering and combination rather than a fundamentally new algorithmic insight, and the paper could better discuss overlap with the concurrent/prior DivPrune approach that also uses diversity-based pruning.

The efficiency gains from Stage 2 (relevance-driven full token removal) appear marginal for standard benchmarks with short answers (Table 4), and the paper explicitly acknowledges this, meaning the practical benefit of the second stage is mostly hypothetical for realistic short-answer VQA/benchmark settings and only anecdotally demonstrated for long-form generation (single case study, no quantitative long-generation latency/accuracy table).

Some hyperparameters (threshold τ=0.03, candidate layers at L/2, 5L/8, 6L/8, 7L/8) appear tuned specifically for LLaVA-NeXT-7B/13B and Vicuna-based decoders; it is unclear how sensitive these choices are when transferred to substantially different LLM backbones or decoder depths, which could limit out-of-the-box generalizability despite the training-free claim.

The main comparison table excludes some baselines (FastV, SparseVLM) from the 13B setting due to reported transferability issues, and GlobalCom2 is excluded from video benchmarks; while explained, this makes some comparisons less complete.
